content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone know how to display and save analog values from [company_name] [product_name] (with [product_name] and internet) and [product_name] Unified (SCADA)? Thank you. [user_name]

[product_name] Unified is not compatible with [product_name]. [product_name] can be used as a router for [product_name]. For storing values, I suggest using the Data Log feature within [product_name].

Is compatibility possible even via TCP/IP? I also saw videos on YouTube that selected [product_name] as the communication Modbus and used digital inputs—how was this achieved? Are there third-party solutions available?

Since [product_name] Unified isn't officially released for [product_name], another solution might be better. It's possible that something works, but future updates or lack of official compatibility could break the setup. Note: Generally, [product_name] [version_no] or newer supports Modbus TCP. One alternative is to create a simple SCADA system for [product_name] using [product_name] Web Editor. The required webserver is included; just activate it (via the Tools > Transfer > Access control menu). Alternatively, use a [product_name] PLC with [product_name] Unified.
Thank you for your response. I have [product_name] Web Editor set up and am using a [product_name] PLC with [product_name] Unified. So, using Modbus TCP should work?
A user mentioned that this connection works: Unified Panel to [product_name] Connection - [article_no] - Industry Support [company_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to display and store analog values from [company_name] [product_name] devices (equipped with [product_name] and internet access) in [product_name] Unified SCADA. There is ongoing discussion about the (in)compatibility between these products, questions around connections using TCP/IP or Modbus, references to video demonstrations, and suggestions for alternative solutions.
